questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the highlighted word segment in the given sentence. If the sentence is grammatically correct, select ‘No correction’.

The boy **play **football since he has come from school.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. has been playing .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence refers to an ongoing action that started in the past and continues in the present, indicated by the phrase "since he has come from school."
 
• To express such ongoing actions, the **present perfect continuous tense** is used.
 
• The structure of the present perfect continuous tense is **has/have been + verb-ing**.

Correct sentence: *The boy **has been playing** football since he has come from school*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Present Perfect Tense:**

 
 
• **Structure:** has/have + past participle.
 
• **Example:** He has completed his homework.
 
• **Usage:** Refers to actions that are completed in the past but have relevance to the present.
 
 
 
• **Past Continuous Tense:**
 
 
• **Structure:** was/were + verb-ing.
 
• **Example:** He was playing football when it started raining.
 
• **Usage:** Refers to actions that were ongoing at a specific time in the past.

questions.question:
The given sentence is divided into four segments. Select the option that has the segment with an adverbial usage error.

Mrs. Jennifer, / our English professor, / told us that the wind / reluctantly rustled the branches.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. reluctantly rustled the branches. .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"reluctantly"** is an adverb used to describe unwilling or hesitant actions.
 
• In the given context, the wind "rustling" the branches cannot logically be described as reluctant because the wind is not sentient and cannot feel hesitation.
 
• Thus, the adverbial usage of **"reluctantly"** in this context is incorrect.

Correct sentence: *Mrs. Jennifer, our English professor, told us that the wind rustled the branches.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Adverbs:**

 
 
• **Definition:** Words that modify verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs, often indicating manner, time, place, frequency, or degree.
 
• **Example:** She sings beautifully. (Here, "beautifully" modifies the verb "sings.")
 
 
 
• **Common Errors in Adverb Usage:**
 
 
• Using adverbs where they do not logically fit, as in this case with "reluctantly."
 
• Incorrect placement of adverbs, which can lead to confusion in meaning.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the given sentence.

Give the cake to __which __asks for it first.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2 i.e. Whoever**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"whomever"** is used as an object pronoun in a sentence. It refers to "whoever" in situations where it is the object of the verb or preposition. (जिसको भी)

 
 
• **Example:** You can give the prize to whomever you like.
 
 
 
• The word **"whoever"** is a subject pronoun and is used to mean "any person who." It functions as the subject of the verb in the sentence. (जो कोई भी)
 
 
• **Example:** Whoever finishes the race first will win a prize.
 
 
 
• In the given sentence, "Give the cake to which asks for it first," the word "whoever" correctly substitutes "which" because the subject of the sentence needs a pronoun that refers to "any person who."

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2 i.e. Whoever**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Whomever** (जिसको भी): Used when referring to the object of a sentence or clause.

 
 
• **Example:** She will help whomever needs assistance.
 
 
 
• **Whomsoever** (जिस किसी को भी): A formal version of "whomever," used to refer to the object in a sentence.
 
 
• **Example:** The award will be given to whomsoever the committee chooses.
 
 
 
• **Whichever** (जो भी): Refers to one or a few options from a group.
 
 
• **Example:** You can pick whichever dress you like for the party.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**effectively**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage discusses the benefits of time management.
 
• The word to fill the blank should describe *how* people manage their time to achieve their goals.
 
• "Effectively" means in a way that produces the intended result, which accurately describes successful time management.
 
• The other options do not accurately describe the manner in which time is managed.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

 

Complete Passage: *Effective time management is (1) crucial__ for success. By prioritising tasks, individuals can enhance (2)__**productivity**__ and reduce stress. Planning allows for a balance (3) __**between **__work and personal life. Studies show that those who manage their time (4) __**effectively **__are more likely to achieve their goals. It is a skill (5)____positively impacts both professional and personal aspects of life.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Efficient** (कुशल): "Efficient" means doing something in a way that achieves the maximum productivity with minimum wasted effort or expense. While related to good time management, it doesn't describe the *action* of managing time.
 
• **Strongly** (मजबूती से): "Strongly" means in a powerful way, which doesn't fit the context of managing time.
 
• **Excitedly** (उत्तेजित रूप से): "Excitedly" means in a way that shows enthusiasm, which is irrelevant to how time is managed.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**which**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage concludes by describing time management as a skill.
 
• The word to fill the blank should introduce a relative clause that describes the skill.
 
• "Which" is the correct relative pronoun to refer to a skill.
 
• The other options are not appropriate for referring to a skill in this context.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

 

Complete Passage: *Effective time management is (1) crucial__ for success. By prioritising tasks, individuals can enhance (2) __**productivity **__and reduce stress. Planning allows for a balance (3) __**between **__work and personal life. Studies show that those who manage their time (4) __**effectively **__are more likely to achieve their goals. It is a skill (5) __**which **__positively impacts both professional and personal aspects of life.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Those** (वे): "Those" is a demonstrative pronoun used to refer to people, not a skill.
 
• **What** (क्या): "What" is an interrogative pronoun or a relative pronoun that introduces a noun clause, not an adjective clause describing a skill.
 
• **Whereby** (जिसके द्वारा): "Whereby" is an adverb that means "by which" or "in accordance with which," and does not fit the context of describing a skill.
